claims.text: The family of 19-year-old Arpit, who was killed in the Satya Niketan PG building collapse, donated his corneas.

Delhi Police arrested retired Indian Air Force Sergeant Hariram Gupta, aged 81, his wife Urmila Gupta, aged 75, and their son Mahesh Gupta, aged 52, in connection with the Satya Niketan building collapse.
The Satya Niketan property where the collapse occurred is registered in the name of Urmila Gupta, while Hariram Gupta and Mahesh Gupta managed and operated the paying guest facility.
Basement renovation work and water accumulation likely contributed to the collapse of the Satya Niketan building.
Rescue agencies rescued 12 people from the collapsed Satya Niketan building, of whom seven died.
The 55-year-old, five-storey building in Satya Niketan housed a boys' paying guest facility with two rooms per floor and two beds per room.
A police source cited by PTI stated that the 55-square-metre structure had no columns or beams for support.
A case was filed against the accused at the South Campus Police Station under charges of culpable homicide, negligence in upkeep of a structure, and endangering safety.
The Delhi government ordered a citywide sealing of illegal five-storey buildings following the Satya Niketan collapse.
The Cockroach Janta Party released a list of seven demands following the Satya Niketan collapse, calling for a probe into the larger PG mafia and the construction of government hostels.
Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das requested compensation of up to 1 crore rupees for families of the deceased and 20 lakh rupees for the injured.

Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das questioned Delhi Urban Development & Planning and Education Minister Ashish Sood on why 13 district committees constituted after a June 2026 hotel fire were wound down.
The Delhi High Court directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi to conduct an inquiry at the highest executive level into the Satya Niketan collapse.
A Delhi High Court bench of Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia observed that responsibility for the mishap extends to university authorities and the MCD, not solely the PG owner.

An alleged agreement signed by occupants of the Satya Niketan property stated that PG authorities are not responsible for casualties or compensation due to sealing, fire, heavy rains, earthquakes, or natural calamities.
The MCD had flagged the collapsed Satya Niketan structure as an unauthorized G+4 building in a resettlement colony where permission was only granted for a G+1 structure.
The Delhi High Court directed the MCD to audit PGs and hostels and asked Delhi University for details on outstation students and hostel capacity.
Following the collapse of the 40-to-50-year-old building in Satya Niketan, 11 people were rescued and an estimated 30 to 35 students remained trapped under rubble.
Five municipal officials were suspended following the Satya Niketan building collapse.
The owner of the collapsed Satya Niketan building was arrested in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan.
